skill.name: writing-video-scripts
skill.description: Writes spoken video scripts that fit supplied clip durations and visual beats. It creates hooks, controls pacing, and divides one monologue into clip-ready segments.
skill.summary: Creates natural video scripts sized and segmented for exact clip durations.
skill.author: supercmohq

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives caused by ordinary video-script terminology about spoken words and on-screen content. No system reconnaissance, prompt injection, data exfiltration, or other security concern was found.

static_findings.snippet: description: Writes what is said in a video — the words a person speaks on camera, or a voiceover he
- which beats of the story land in which clip — what happens on screen, not what gets said
**Write only what can be said aloud.** Commas and full stops are what a reader turns into breath, so

finding_verdicts.reason: The description defines spoken dialogue and voiceover output for videos. It does not request or perform inspection of system information.
The text asks which story beats appear in each video clip so the script matches the footage. This is creative context gathering, not system reconnaissance.
The instruction limits output to words that a narrator can speak aloud. It concerns script formatting and contains no system discovery behavior.

content.user_title: Write Video Scripts That Fit Every Clip
content.value_statement: Video scripts often exceed runtime limits or conflict with the footage. This skill writes natural spoken copy that fits each clip and visual beat.
actual_capabilities: Calculates target word counts from supplied clip durations.
Writes opening hooks that connect to the first visual beat.
Creates one continuous monologue in a natural spoken style.
Splits the monologue into ordered segments for individual clips.
Checks each segment against timing limits and on-screen action.
limitations: Requires total runtime, clip durations, visual beats, delivery mode, and approved claims.
Produces text only and does not record audio or create video.
Does not invent product claims, evidence, or social proof.
Does not add music guidance unless the user requests it.

use_cases.title: Plan Social Video Voiceovers
use_cases.description: Create a paced voiceover that follows the visual sequence of a short social video.

use_cases.title: Script Product Demonstrations
use_cases.description: Turn approved product facts and demonstration beats into concise spoken segments.

use_cases.title: Prepare Creator Dialogue
use_cases.description: Write natural on-camera dialogue that fits each recorded or planned clip.

prompt_templates.title: Write a Single-Clip Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Write an on-camera script for a [duration]-second clip. The visual shows [beat]. Use only this approved claim: [claim].
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs spoken copy for one short clip.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Voiceover Sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a [total duration]-second voiceover across [number] clips. Use these clip durations and visual beats: [details]. Keep the delivery conversational.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user has a planned sequence and needs timed narration.

prompt_templates.title: Choose and Build a Hook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a script using a [hook pattern] opening. Match this first visual: [visual]. Preserve these approved facts: [facts]. Segment by [durations].
prompt_templates.scenario: A marketer needs a specific opening strategy and complete script.

prompt_templates.title: Revise a Timed Multi-Clip Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Revise this script for natural speech and exact clip timing: [script]. Use [durations] and [visual beats]. Preserve wording of these claims: [claims].
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs timing, continuity, and claim control across an existing draft.

output_examples.input: Write a 12-second voiceover for two six-second clips showing whole beans, then a brewed cup. Approved fact: roasted weekly.
output_examples.output:
Clip 1: These beans did not wait months on a shelf. They were roasted this week.

Clip 2: Grind them fresh, brew your cup, and taste what weekly roasting changes.

output_examples.input: Write a 15-second on-camera skincare script. Show the nearly empty jar, application, then the finished look. No product claims.
output_examples.output:
Clip 1: This jar has one use left, so let us make it count.

Clip 2: A small amount, pressed in slowly.

Clip 3: That is the finished look, simple and ready.

best_practices: Provide exact clip durations and describe what appears in every clip.
Supply approved claims and evidence before requesting the script.
Read each segment aloud at a natural pace before recording.
anti_patterns: Do not request invented statistics, testimonials, or product claims.
Do not omit timing details and expect precise segment lengths.
Do not combine unrelated hook patterns in the same opening.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide total runtime, each clip duration, visual beats, delivery mode, and any approved claims.

faq.question: Can it write both voiceover and on-camera dialogue?
faq.answer: Yes. State the delivery mode so the wording matches how the script will be spoken.

faq.question: How does it keep scripts within the runtime?
faq.answer: It targets two to three words per second and checks every segment against its clip duration.

faq.question: Will it create claims about my product?
faq.answer: No. It uses only supplied claims and observable details from the described footage.

faq.question: Does it generate audio or video?
faq.answer: No. It returns written spoken segments only.

faq.question: Can it revise an existing script?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the draft, clip timings, visual beats, and any wording that must remain unchanged.
